issues.description: Global symbol 'display_start' (framebuffer base) is declared and used in the problem and template but is missing in the solution while still being referenced. Problem statement refers to the framebuffer base 'display_start' as the start of the screen buffer used by set_pixel. The template (pixel.asm) declares 'display_start RESB 8294400' in .bss. The solution file contains a comment saying 'display_start moved to local stack scope in main' and does not declare the global buffer, yet the solution still references the identifier 'display_start' (e.g. 'add eax, display_start' in set_pixel and 'mov esi, display_start' in main). This creates an undefined symbol in the solution, causing assembly/link errors and preventing the code from compiling or running as intended, blocking students from using the provided solution as a reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Either restore a global framebuffer symbol in the solution to match the template (e.g. add 'section .bss' and 'display_start RESB 8294400') so references like 'add eax, display_start' assemble, or consistently implement the intended move-to-stack design: allocate the framebuffer base on the stack or in a local variable and update all references in set_pixel and main to use the computed address (pass it in a register or store it in a known register/stack slot). Ensure the solution and template agree on where and how 'display_start' is defined so students can assemble and run the example without undefined symbol errors.
